claim: People hold a framework against a few clashes: with brief exposure they report the expected object (dominance), and recognising an anomaly needs about 4x the exposure of normal items (114 ms vs 28 ms, N=28).
agent_test: Show the agent items that violate its stated frame; measure turns to first explicit anomaly note at equal tokens. Primary evidence is one 1949 study; a 2011 replication was mixed and unread (a11). Horner and Tung 2011 (d02) did not reproduce resistance: slowdown in mixed sets reflects uncertainty, with trial-and-error responding.

claim: A few repeated clashes weaken the expectation: incongruous-card threshold fell from 360 ms (no prior) to 230 after one trick card and 84 after two or three; prior normal cards gave no gain (420 ms, n.s.).
agent_test: Dose-response: trigger frame review after k=1,2,3 independent failures and compare solve rate at equal tokens. Horner and Tung (d02) reported equal difficulty for trick and regular cards in pure sets; the 1949 dose-response is not a safe basis for N.

claim: Theory-preserving responses dominate when a belief is entrenched; data are judged through the theory (6 of 10 rival-theory proponents accepted anomalous data vs 4 of 32 holders), but data are not wholly theory-laden (discount measure r=-.46 predicts belief change).
agent_test: Plant a contradicting observation after the agent commits to a frame; log which of Chinn and Brewer's 7 responses it uses. One lab, N=64; numbers not re-opened this pass (PDF blocked).

claim: Having an alternative theory available did NOT increase belief change in Chinn and Brewer (.97 vs .72 drop, F<1), against the Kuhn idea that crisis resolves only when a rival is available.
agent_test: Test whether offering a candidate alternative frame at the trigger raises switch rate vs 'reconsider the frame' with no alternative. Small N, null result, low power.

claim: Real scientists attend to surprise rather than explain it away: in one lab 176 group interactions followed unexpected findings vs 23 for expected; timing and target matter (early surprise about an auxiliary assumption is ignored).
agent_test: Sort failures by auxiliary vs core assumption; escalate to frame review only for core-assumption failures. b20 is secondhand, so independence is partial.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Groups catch reasoning errors that individuals make; in one HIV lab talk 7 of 11 inductions were modified or dropped by others.
agent_test: Compare single-agent revision vs a separate critic call at equal tokens.

claim: Kuhn gives no number for how many anomalies make a crisis; a failure-count threshold is our design choice, not a Kuhn finding. Kuhn 1962 ch. IX read in primary text (d01): no count; he points to the extent and stubbornness of the anomaly.
agent_test: Sweep N in {1,2,3,5} consecutive independent failures; mark the chosen N as [D].

claim: Scientific fields show Kuhnian lock-in at scale: from 1,000 to 100,000 papers per year the predicted top-50 rank correlation between adjacent years rises 0.25 to 0.74, and in Electrical Engineering the top 1% citation share rose 8.6% to 16.7% as the field grew.
agent_test: Not directly testable on an agent; supports the point that dropping a frame is costly and rare.

claim: Models of theory change (explanatory coherence, system dynamics, Lakatos progressive vs degenerating) give switch criteria based on explanatory gain or falling progress, not counts of failures.
agent_test: Implement a Lakatos-style rule (switch when patches only fit old facts and predict nothing new) vs a count rule at equal tokens. Several lines are from memory or unread.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction by LLMs does not reliably help and often hurts; with an oracle stop signal it helps (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3 with oracle; 75.9 to 74.7 after two intrinsic rounds).
agent_test: The failure trigger must use external signals (tests, verifiers), not the model's own judgment. Compare self-judged vs external trigger.

claim: The bottleneck in LLM revision is locating the error, not fixing it: GPT-4 finds the first wrong step 52.87% of the time, while backtracking with the true location repairs many traces.
agent_test: Give the agent the failing step location vs none and compare repair rate.

claim: Resampling explains much of the apparent gain from feedback in graph colouring: self-critique reaches about 40% any-time-correct, equal to sound-verifier runs.
agent_test: Always compare a frame switch against plain best-of-N at equal tokens.

claim: Retry-with-lesson loops with an external success signal improve results (Reflexion: ALFWorld 130 of 134 in 12 trials; ReAct alone plateaus between trials 6 and 7).
agent_test: Lesson memory across trials at equal tokens; this is a retry, not a frame switch.

claim: Reasoning models switch lines of thought too much: wrong answers have 418% more thought switches and 225% more tokens; penalising switches raises AIME24 pass@1 for QwQ 38.3 to 44.1. A frame switch must be gated, not frequent.
agent_test: Enforce a minimum commit length before switching and measure accuracy. Single paper; effect small for stronger models (R1 73.8 to 74.8). Wang's prompt-only persistence arm did not help R1 (73.8 to 72.4; d12); use a mechanism, not an instruction.

claim: LLMs under-test their hypotheses: confirming tests dominate; success ranged 6% to 78% across 11 models (Wason-style); confirmation share correlates with failure (rho -0.779, FalsifyBench); opposite-test prompts raised success (Qwen3-32B thinking 0.41 to 0.61).
agent_test: Add a falsification-test operator before frame defence; measure incompatible:compatible test ratio and success.

claim: LLM agents rarely revise on contradicting evidence: ignored evidence in 68% of 619 chemistry tasks and changed output in 26% (press report); in altered-physics scenes the top model discovered 16.7%, others 0%.
agent_test: Inject a planted anomaly mid-run and measure uptake with and without a trigger. c14 is a press article; c15 numbers were not re-verified.

claim: Prediction can be right while the stated law is wrong, so a failure counter based on prediction error alone can miss a wrong frame.
agent_test: Track an explanation score separately from fit; trigger on both.

claim: Code-tool access can push strong models to exploit too early (GPT-5 72.9 to 69.6) while helping weak ones (GPT-4.1 5.3 to 16.1).
agent_test: Delay exploitation until k alternative frames have been tried.

claim: A runtime monitor that detects a regime change and expands the hypothesis space cut premature answers (exactly-N submissions 28.0% to 6.0%) but did not significantly raise accuracy (93.9% to 95.3%).
agent_test: Closest test of a switch trigger; one model (Sonnet 4.5), synthetic task.

claim: Holding several competing models and turning recurring discrepancies into correction rules raised discovery (GPT-5.4 pass@1 1.86% to 38.08%), but BoxingGym shows prior information can hurt, so benefit is task-dependent.
agent_test: Single-frame vs multi-frame hold at equal tokens.

claim: The only direct LLM test of a Kuhn-style trigger (Smith 2026) does not support it: the Kuhn agent fired after N non-improving runs (63 runs, 33.5M of 229.0M tokens), the paper says its structure was non-load-bearing vs a simple control statement, the Phase 1 to 2 gain (0.664 to 0.846) came from infrastructure fixes, and a floor prompt beat the full scaffold (0.8896 vs 0.7942).
agent_test: Isolate the trigger: same loop with and without a fresh-context reframing at plateau, equal tokens, several tasks. Smith's loops also lost to best-of-15 fresh draws in 7 of 10 arms (d05).

claim: Restart-after-3-failures with fresh context carrying only lessons is a practitioner rule with no measured support (figures labelled illustrative).
agent_test: Fresh-context restart vs continued context after 3 failures.

claim: Rigidity is a known LLM failure as in people: few-shot exact match GPT-4o 0.33 to 0.66 when complex examples come first; on Einstellung-style medical items models scored 48-52% vs physicians 66%.
agent_test: Order problems shortcut-first vs complex-first and measure the switch to the better method.

claim: Anomaly handling in people depends on the cause they attribute (N=6 think-aloud); weak evidence only.
agent_test: Require a stated cause attribution before the keep/drop/switch decision.

claim: Bibliometric signals flag past paradigm shifts after the fact (AUROC 0.969 on 16 pairs), but citation features alone matched the full multi-agent workflow.
agent_test: Not relevant to a trigger inside one agent.

claim: A plateau is not proof of a wrong frame: in Smith 2026 a 49-run no-improvement stall came from a mismatched benchmark and deleted diagnostics, fixed by infrastructure, not by reframing.
agent_test: Before reframing at plateau, check signal validity and that the agent can see per-case failures. Compare reframe-at-plateau with signal-repair at plateau.

claim: Self-judged progress is unreliable: an agent called all 54 cycles improvements, 56% had zero or negative measured change; the strongest in-band judge accepted 44% regressions and rejected 38% of real gains. A bare external accept/reject verdict gave similar output to full feedback.
agent_test: Count failures from tests or a verifier, not from the agent's verdict. Compare self-judged vs external counter at equal tokens. Park and Choi is a preprint pilot (one agent).

claim: The 1949 card study that Kuhn used is not a safe base: Horner and Tung 2011 (two experiments) found equal identification of trick and regular cards in pure sets, slowdown only in mixed sets, and trial-and-error responding, inconsistent with resistance to incongruity.
agent_test: Do not assume an agent clings to a frame by default; measure uptake of planted anomalies (c14, c15) rather than assume it. Abstract only; numbers unread.

claim: Triggers that fire on any anomaly also over-fire: in normal-physics controls 36.1% of LLM reports claimed an altered law without support, while only one of 12 models found the real one (16.7%); a concrete scene clue lifted discovery to 28.6% and five times the turns did not.
agent_test: Report false-alarm rate with any trigger; compare 'reconsider' vs 'reconsider with a candidate alternative'. Preprint; model names unchecked.

claim: A Lakatos-style rule (does the latest patch predict something new that holds?) is defined in the philosophy but has no LLM test found; the nearest operational signals are days-flat outcome counts and a core-assumption registry (unvalidated design notes).
agent_test: Implement 'new-fact prediction rate of patches' as the signal and compare with a failure counter at equal tokens.
